messages:
chandra: FYI, after we enabled mixed fp8-int4 kernels on dedicated-pool-7 we are seeing structured JSON tests flip on trailing commas and missing numeric fields in a subset of eval cases.

anjali: when did the rollout happen and was it canary-first?

chandra: rollout started 2025-11-02T22:41:05Z, canary for 2 hours then auto promoted. deploy-bot logs:

deploy-bot: rollout mixed-quant-v1 -> dedicated-pool-7 completed at 2025-11-02T22:43:29Z

maria: repro run shows eval-suite v3 delta +9.3% on structured-json; most diffs clustered on punctuation tokens and integer fields being dropped.

lisa: any kernel timing changes? maybe batching heuristics shifted and we get smaller batches, exposing numeric instability.

chandra: profiler excerpt for one failing request (p95 path):

``
kernel: attn_fp8_short       8.9ms  (old fp16: 5.0ms)
kernel: gemm_int4            1.7ms
kernel: attn_fp16_fallback  25.2ms (triggered for seq>1500)
KV cache hit-rate: 82% -> 56% post-roll
avg_batch_size: 4.1 -> 2.1
```

maria: KV miss spike stands out. I dumped cache key hex for pairs and saw occasional mismatches where padding bytes differ after quantization.

anjali: padding semantics differ? we recently changed compaction for int4 to trim trailing zeros.

derek: that could explain mismatches. cache key bytes need to be invariant across quant modes. If padding normalization isn't applied pre-quant, int4 path can produce different key bytes.

chandra: also noticed more fallback_attn_freq for long contexts — kernel selection rules currently pick fp8 for short seqs and fallback to fp16 for long; mixed path creates different internal rounding and sometimes token drop around commas.

lisa: token probs around structural tokens are very sensitive. Maria, can you run per-token KL and token-prob waterfall for punctuation and numerics?

maria: on it. preliminary: mean KL for commas increased from 0.02 to 0.31; numeric tokens (digits) KL increased to 0.18. Also entropy for '}' ']' tokens up.

derek: plan suggested:
- hotfix: rollback mixed-quant-v1 from pool-7
- add a hash-assert on KV cache keys across quant modes
- add opt-in flag to force unified kernel path (fp16-only) for repro
- add padding normalization in quant encoder path
- run synthetic heavy-batching reproducer to surface nondeterminism

chandra: agree. also let's try a narrower re-roll: enable fp8 only for attention-short kernel and keep matmuls in fp16 to minimize numeric drift.

anjali: I'll open PR for padding normalization + unit tests to assert cache-key equality across dtype conversions.

deploy-bot: rollback mixed-quant-v1 -> dedicated-pool-7 initiated by derek at 2025-11-02T23:05:02Z

deploy-bot: rollback complete at 2025-11-02T23:09:18Z :white_check_mark:

maria: uploaded per-token diffs: /shared/evals/mixquant/per_token_kl.csv and cache-key-dumps to /shared/infra/kv-key-diffs.txt

lisa: once PR is up tag me. Also add a canary that forces common kernel selection for long/short paths so we can A/B the numeric impact.

derek: will schedule A/B runs and surface latency/cost tradeoffs. keeping thread open until re-roll passes structured tests.
